newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank Montreal CEO earns C$3.85 mln in '96.
newsitem.headline: Bank Montreal CEO earns C$3.85 mln in '96.

text.p: Bank of Montreal chairman and chief executive officer Matthew Barrett took home a C$3.85 million pay packet in 1996, the bank said on Thursday.
Barrett's compensation was up sharply from C$2.49 million in 1995, due mostly to bigger incentive payouts after a year of record bank profits and soaring stock prices.

Canada's third largest bank rolled up a record C$1.16 billion profit in the year ended October 31, up 18.4 percent from 1995. Bank of Montreal's return on equity improved to 17 percent in 1996 from 15.4 percent last year, while its stock climbed 36 percent during the year.
The compensation figures were included in a circular released by the bank on Thursday.
Barrett's pay packet included a base salary of C$900,000, unchanged from last year -- and a C$1.3 million bonus, up C$100,000 from the previous year.
Barrett also took home C$1.65 million as a result of the strong performance of the bank's stock. He earned C$390,000 from stock appreciation rights in 1995.
Bank of Montreal is the first of Canada's Big Six banks to report its 1996 executive compensation. The five other banks are expected to report over the next month.
Among other senior Bank of Montreal executives, Brian Steck, vice-chairman of corporate and investment banking, earned a total of C$2.9 million in 1996, up from C$2.5 million the previous year.

President and chief operating officer Anthony Comper received C$2.2 million in 1996, up from C$1.5 million last year. Alan McNally, chief executive officer of the bank's U.S. unit Harris Bankcorp Inc, earned C$1.8 million this year, up from C$1.3 million in 1995.
Bank of Montreal's annual shareholders meeting will be held on January 21 in St. John's, Newfoundland.
